newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA LATE RUBBER STABLE, S.KOREA BUYS.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA LATE RUBBER STABLE, S.KOREA BUYS.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices were mostly stable in late trading on Tuesday, with a South Korean tyre-maker buying October shipments.
Traders said the South Korean player bought several hundred tonnes at 43.50 cents/lb fob Medan.
"I sold them a few hundred tonnes," one trader said, declining to give the exact amount. "The tyre-maker has also been buying from other sellers in Medan."
A fall in the Indonesian rupiah against the U.S. dollar saw Singapore dealers bidding at well below offer prices.

"The dealers were bidding at 42.25 cents for October and 42.75 cents for November shipments," one trader said. "They are of the view that prices in Indonesia should be lower because we will now be getting more rupiah per U.S. dollar."
"I found the bids too low, and no deals were done."
Traders said a sharp decline in the Malaysian ringgit made prices there comparatively lower than Indonesian values.
"The SMR grade in Malaysia is at an about 1.5-cent discount to Indonesian rubber," one trader said.
Traders said October shipment SIR20 was mostly offered unchanged at 43.50 cents/lb fob Medan and 43.00-43.25 cents fob Palembang and Padang.
